title: Lima bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs, Causes and the Fertilizer That Fixes It
metaTitle: Lima bean Nutrient Deficiency: Signs and Fertilizer Fix
metaDescription: Lima bean nutrient deficiency shows in the leaves. See the signs of nitrogen and phosphorus in patani, how to be sure, and the fertilizer to apply.
excerpt: Lima bean nutrient deficiency is one of the first things to check when the leaves of your patani (lima bean) turn yellow, purple or burnt at the edges. On Philippine farms the usual ones are nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, manganese, zinc and boron. This guide shows where each one starts, how to be sure, and the fertilizer that fixes it.

heroImage.credit: Maja Dumat, CC BY 2.0, via Flickr

blocks.text: Start with one question: did the change begin on the old leaves or on the young ones? Nitrogen, phosphorus and potassium move inside the plant, so a shortage shows on the old, lower leaves first. But manganese, zinc and boron stay where the plant first put them, so the young leaves and the growing tip show it first. After that, the color and the pattern narrow down which lima bean nutrient deficiency you have, and a soil test confirms it. Each one below has its signs, its causes and its fix.

blocks.text: Before you buy fertilizer for a lima bean nutrient deficiency

So use the table to pick the likeliest lima bean nutrient deficiency, then read its section below. Also keep in mind that dry soil, standing water, cold nights, a pest or a disease can look the same. That is why it pays to check the roots and the whole field first.
Nitrogen deficiency in lima bean

Lower leaves turn pale yellow first and the plant stays light green and slow, with few pods. Patani makes most of its nitrogen in root nodules, so this usually means the nodules failed. You see it most at this stage: three to six weeks after planting.
Why nitrogen deficiency happens in patani

In a legume this usually means poor nodulation: no inoculant in a field new to the crop, inoculant killed by sun or heat, very acid soil, waterlogging, hot dry soil, or too much nitrogen fertilizer near the seed, which stops nodules from forming.
How to tell it apart

Manganese deficiency yellows between green veins on young leaves, common on limed soils. Sulfur deficiency starts on the newest leaves. To be sure, dig, do not pull, a few plants 3 to 6 weeks after planting, wash the roots and cut some nodules open. Pink to red inside means they are working, white means not active yet, and brown, grey or mushy means dead.
What to apply for nitrogen deficiency
Feed the crop with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test. Nodules cannot be added to a standing crop (Texas AandM).

Sold here with nitrogen: **Atlas Granular Urea** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (46 0 0), **YaraVera Viking Ship Granular Urea** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (46 0 0), **Planters Products Granular Urea** by Planters Products, Inc. (46 0 0) and **Harbest Granular Urea** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (46 0 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [urea fertilizer](/blog/urea-fertilizer), and the page on [nitrogen deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/nitrogen-deficiency) in every crop. In anee.io, Anee, the [smart farm technician](/features/ai-agricultural-technician), reads a photo of the leaf and tells you which nutrient is short.
To keep it away, inoculate seed with the right Rhizobium inoculant, keep it shaded and avoid heavy nitrogen near the seed.
Phosphorus deficiency in lima bean
Plants stay short with dark bluish green leaves, sometimes with purple or bronze tints. Growth and flowering are slow and pods are few. You see it most at this stage: seedling to flowering.
Why phosphorus deficiency happens in patani
Acid soils and soils low in phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Nitrogen deficiency makes plants pale, not dark. To be sure, soil test for phosphorus.
What to apply for phosphorus deficiency
Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop, give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

Sold here with phosphorus: **Triple Super Phosphate** by Newman Chemicals Corporation (0 46 0), **Sagrex Duofos Granular Guano Phosphate** by Sagrex Corporation (0 22 0 (guano phosphate)), **Philphos 18 46 0** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0 (diammonium phosphate)) and **Atlas Di Ammonium Phosphate** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (18 46 0). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [16 20 0 fertilizer](/blog/16-20-0-fertilizer), and the page on [phosphorus deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/phosphorus-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, apply phosphorus at planting each season.
Potassium deficiency in lima bean
The edges of the older leaves turn yellow and then scorched and brown. As it gets worse the leaves turn fully yellow and drop. You see it most at this stage: flowering and pod fill.
Why potassium deficiency happens in patani
Sandy soils and soils cropped without potash.
How to tell it apart
Magnesium deficiency yellows between the veins instead of at the edges. To be sure, soil test for potassium.
What to apply for potassium deficiency
Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test.

Sold here with potassium: **Atlas Muriate of Potash** by Atlas Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Philphos Muriate of Potash** by Philippine Phosphate Fertilizer Corporation (0 0 60), **Harbest Granular Muriate of Potash** by Harbest Agribusiness Corporation (0 0 60) and **Swire Muriate of Potash** by Swire Agrotech Agricultural Products Inc. (0 0 60). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [potash fertilizer](/blog/potash-fertilizer), and the page on [potassium deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/potassium-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, include potash at planting on sandy soils.
Manganese deficiency in lima bean
The top leaves turn yellow between the veins, which stay green. Brown spots can follow. Lima bean is one of the crops that need the most manganese. You see it most at this stage: early to mid growth.
Why manganese deficiency happens in patani
High pH soils, sandy soils limed too much, and soils high in organic matter that stay wet.
How to tell it apart
Iron deficiency turns the veins yellow too. Zinc deficiency looks much the same in beans. To be sure, leaf test for manganese and a soil pH test.
What to apply for manganese deficiency

The University of Wisconsin gives about 5.6 kg of manganese per hectare (5 pounds per acre) as manganese sulfate to the soil, or about 1.1 kg per hectare as a spray, sometimes two or three times. Do not put chelated manganese in the soil. It can make things worse.

Sold here with manganese: **Manganese Sulfate** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (31 percent manganese), **Tierramino Mn** by Unilox Far East Resources Inc. (12 percent manganese and 7 percent N), **Multimate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (1.8 percent Mn, 2.8 percent Zn, 4 percent N, 4.5 percent S (w/v)) and **Biozome** by Manchem Industries, Inc. (12 percent S, 12 percent Zn, 3 percent Mn, 1 percent Mg, 1 percent Fe, 1 percent Cu, 0.5 percent B, 0.05 percent Mo). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [manganese deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/manganese-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, do not over lime, and test soil pH before each crop.
Zinc deficiency in lima bean

Leaves turn yellowish between green veins and dead patches appear if it is severe. Internodes stay short and leaves small, and fewer pods set. You see it most at this stage: early growth to flowering.
Why zinc deficiency happens in patani
Soils above pH 6.5, over limed sands and heavy phosphorus.
How to tell it apart
Manganese deficiency is very hard to tell apart in beans. A leaf test settles it. To be sure, leaf test for zinc and a soil pH test.
What to apply for zinc deficiency

Give 5 to 10 kg zinc sulfate per hectare to the soil or a 0.5 percent zinc sulfate spray (5 g per liter) for beans. The University of Wisconsin keeps sprays at about 0.7 kg zinc sulfate per hectare to avoid leaf burn.

Sold here with zinc: **Harvester Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Universal Harvester, Inc. (22 percent zinc), **Great Planters Zinc Sulphate Heptahydrate** by Agway Chemicals Corp. (21 percent zinc), **Zinc Sulphate Monohydrate** by Petbowe Trading Corporation (33 percent zinc) and **YaraVita ZINTRAC 700** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (40 percent zinc). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [fertilizer with zinc](/blog/micronutrients-for-rice), and the page on [zinc deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/zinc-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, mix zinc into the basal fertilizer on high pH soils.
Boron deficiency in lima bean
Young leaves curl and crinkle and the growing tip stays small. Flowering and pod set suffer. You see it most at this stage: flowering.
Why boron deficiency happens in patani
Sandy soils low in organic matter, high pH soils and drought.
How to tell it apart
Virus diseases also crinkle leaves, but with a mosaic pattern. To be sure, leaf or soil test for boron.
What to apply for boron deficiency
Give a 0.2 percent borax spray (2 g per liter) for beans. Never place boron in the seed row. A band is toxic to bean seed (UW).

Sold here with boron: **Solubor** by Caldic Philippines Inc. (21 percent boron), **Etifert 11 (Borax Decahydrate)** by Zetryl.Chem Phils., Inc. (11 percent boron), **YaraVita BORTRAC 150** by Yara Fertilizers Philippines, Inc. (11.1 percent boron) and **Grow More Liquid Chelate Boron** by Sagrex Corporation (10 percent boron). Check the FPA registration on the bag and follow the label rate. For the how and when, see our guide to [foliar fertilizer](/blog/foliar-fertilizer), and the page on [boron deficiency](/nutrient-deficiencies/boron-deficiency) in every crop.
To keep it away, keep organic matter up and water evenly at flowering.

blocks.title: Let a soil test decide the rate
blocks.text: A soil test is the surest check for any lima bean nutrient deficiency. Before you buy, ask your Municipal Agriculture Office where to send a soil sample. The DA regional soil laboratories test soil, and the result says how much of each fertilizer your patani needs. That saves money, because extra fertilizer is money lost.

blocks.text: Lima bean nutrient deficiency questions

items.q: Why are my patani leaves turning yellow?
items.a: The most common cause is nitrogen deficiency: pale, slow plants whose lower leaves yellow, with few working nodules. If the young leaves turn yellow first instead, look at manganese deficiency.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes nitrogen deficiency in lima bean?
items.a: Feed the crop with a light sidedress of Urea 46 0 0 or Complete 14 14 14, following the soil test. Nodules cannot be added to a standing crop (Texas AandM).

items.q: What fertilizer fixes phosphorus deficiency in lima bean?
items.a: Apply 16 20 0 or Complete 14 14 14 at planting, following the soil test. For a standing crop, give a 2 percent DAP 18 46 0 spray (20 g per liter) every 15 days for pulses.

items.q: What fertilizer fixes potassium deficiency in lima bean?
items.a: Apply Muriate of potash 0 0 60 or Complete 14 14 14 following the soil test.

items.q: How do I know which nutrient my patani lacks?
items.a: First look at where the change began, on the old leaves or the young ones, then at the color and the pattern. Next, confirm the lima bean nutrient deficiency with a soil test or a leaf test before you buy fertilizer.
